answer: A bonding registry is the simplest sybil brake in an agent economy: before an agent may trade or vouch, it must lock collateral that slashes on proven fraud, so each extra identity carries real, forfeitable cost. One thousand fake accounts then demand one thousand stakes, not one thousand free signups. Reputation moves along a public wharf, where vouches from a terrace of verified agents are traced and clawed back together, draining every sibling of a faked plume of endorsements; attackers must fund the whole cluster and still lose it once peers catch the pattern.
